Apart from the first working day (AC-02.1.4), what happens to all other answers after submission? Can the employee reopen or correct the questionnaire, for example after a move, a marriage, a new child or a corrected nationality? Or are the answers frozen and only HR can change them, and if so, which answers? Should the derived results (subject to source tax, tariff code, canton, civil status for the fund) be recalculated after a change, as AC-02.2.4 requires for the insurance start date?

Certificate of residence (US-07.2): 'not yet' is a valid answer and produces the normal tariff instead of the cross-border tariff. When the employee hands in the certificate later, who updates the answer, and does the recorded tariff code then change (C1Y → N1Y)? The employee cannot edit after submission, and the HR side is out of scope, so the recorded code could stay wrong. Is that acceptable?

Non-return days for Germany (more than 60) and Liechtenstein (more than 45) are asked 'in the calendar year'. Most new employees start mid-year. Is the threshold for the remaining part of the year, the full calendar year, or pro-rated (for start date and/or part-time work)? The answer changes whether the cross-border tariff or the Liechtenstein result applies.

Permit reminder (AC-08.1.1): every employee living abroad gets the reminder. That includes Swiss citizens living in Germany or Liechtenstein, such as Stefan, who have no Swiss permit. Nationality is not asked of people living abroad, so we cannot exclude them. Is a reminder that does not apply to Swiss cross-border commuters acceptable, or should nationality (or 'Swiss citizen yes/no') also be asked of employees living abroad?

"Kept id permit_type for stability; content reduced to 'C permit yes/no' (D-005)." - Names an internal field id and a stability concern about it in the spec text; field ids and their stability are engineering concerns.

"Required field 'Civil status' (mapped to the fund's list, see rule pension_fund_civil_status)
source tax office: Decides married vs single tariff and the spouse exemption (see rule source_tax_civil_status)" - Refers to internal rule identifiers (snake_case ids) in the business text instead of the rule names.

"The calculator's questions 'main residence in Switzerland?' and 'state of residence' are derived from this answer, not asked again (see rule source_tax_residence)." - Another internal snake_case rule id in the prose.

"they are asked for their first working day as a date (DD.MM.YYYY)" - Prescribes the format in which the employee enters the first working day. The fund's DD.MM.YYYY requirement applies to the insurance start date it receives, not to how the employee enters a date; the input format is a UI choice.

"the employee can add and remove children, and for each child is asked" - Prescribes the interaction pattern (add/remove child blocks, copied from the calculator's buttons). The business need is only that every child is described; how the UI collects them is up to engineering.

"with the country given by its English name (e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany")" - Prescribes how country values are represented, and the trace check notes no source backs it. It reads as a representation choice rather than a stakeholder requirement.

info.message: Does the employee see any computed result: the insurance start date, the tariff code, the Liechtenstein result, or 'not subject to source tax'? Or is everything only recorded for HR? Is there a review or summary of all answers before submission, and a confirmation after it?

Children (US-06.1): if the employee answers 'yes' to having children, must they add at least one child? Is there a maximum number of children? The tariff code has a single child digit, and more than 3 children was never tested in the calculator. What should the code look like with 10 or more counting children?

Are there plausibility rules for dates? For example: date of birth not in the future and a minimum age (apprentices or minors), spouse's date of birth plausible, first working day not in the past or not more than X months ahead. If the first working day is already in the past at submission, which insurance start date applies?

House number is always required (AC-01.2.1). What should employees enter whose address has no house number (rural addresses abroad, named houses, PO-box-only addresses)? Are extra address lines needed for 'c/o' or apartment names, given that HR posts documents to these addresses?

The civil status list (AC-03.1.2) has no 'dissolved registered partnership' and no 'partner deceased', which are official Swiss civil statuses. How should employees in those situations answer, and how are they mapped for the fund and for source tax?
The example table in AC-01.1.1 shows first and last name as 'asked' (not 'required') for an employee living abroad, but the criterion says all three fields are always required. Which is correct?

Several example tables contradict their own criteria or each other. In AC-05.7.2, the M0N and P1Y rows show the source tax result as '–' while the other rows show 'tariff code'. In AC-01.3.2, the Italy row shows Canton '–' instead of 'not asked'. In AC-02.2.4, the Julia example has a single row that does not actually show a change of the first working day. Can these be corrected so they can be used as test cases?

The country list must cover everyone (countries by English name). Which official list should we use, for example the one the fund or HR uses? Should the list also cover nationalities such as stateless persons or refugees, whose nationality is not a country?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: What must be entered in the pension fund's 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required but lists only Swiss cantons; cross-border employees cannot be registered without an answer.
options: Canton of work (e.g. Zurich) for employees abroad
Canton means residence; the fund has a separate way for abroad
Ask the fund to add an 'abroad' option
open_questions.recommendation: Keep asking the canton only from residents (D-002) until a domain expert and Pensionskasse Muster confirm.

open_questions.question: How does Pensionskasse Muster want registered partnerships and separated employees registered (the list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), and does it want the partner's details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Provisional mapping (both entered as Married) could register a wrong civil status.
open_questions.recommendation: Verify with a domain expert / the fund; keep D-003 mapping meanwhile.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's screen ask for a spouse's date of birth (or other fields) for Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Screenshots only show Single and Married; a hidden required field would block registration.
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert obtains a screenshot of the fund's screen for Divorced and Widowed.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the calculator for the paths not explored: residence block for A/B/H tariffs, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and the child-result rows marked inferred?

options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live
open_questions.recommendation: Go-live condition: compare all inferred rows and unexplored paths with the calculator.

open_questions.question: Is the specific nationality (and the spouse's nationality and country of residence) needed by any party, or only whether the person is Swiss / lives in Switzerland?

options: Ask only 'Swiss citizen yes/no' and 'lives in Switzerland yes/no'

For example: date of birth not in the future and a minimum age (apprentices or minors), spouse's date of birth plausible, first working day not in the past or not more than X months ahead. If the first working day is already in the past at submission, which insurance start date applies?

House number is always required (AC-01.2.1). What should employees enter whose address has no house number (rural addresses abroad, named houses, PO-box-only addresses)? Are extra address lines needed for 'c/o' or apartment names, given that HR posts documents to these addresses?

The civil status list (AC-03.1.2) has no 'dissolved registered partnership' and no 'partner deceased', which are official Swiss civil statuses. How should employees in those situations answer, and how are they mapped for the fund and for source tax?
The example table in AC-01.1.1 shows first and last name as 'asked' (not 'required') for an employee living abroad, but the criterion says all three fields are always required. Which is correct?

Several example tables contradict their own criteria or each other. In AC-05.7.2, the M0N and P1Y rows show the source tax result as '–' while the other rows show 'tariff code'. In AC-01.3.2, the Italy row shows Canton '–' instead of 'not asked'. In AC-02.2.4, the Julia example has a single row that does not actually show a change of the first working day. Can these be corrected so they can be used as test cases?

The country list must cover everyone (countries by English name). Which official list should we use, for example the one the fund or HR uses? Should the list also cover nationalities such as stateless persons or refugees, whose nationality is not a country?

already_flagged: OQ-canton-abroad: what to enter in the fund's 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and whether it means canton of residence or of work
OQ-civil-status-partnership: how the fund registers registered partnerships and separated employees, and whether it wants the partner's details
OQ-spouse-dob-other-status: whether the fund requires a spouse's date of birth or other fields for Divorced/Widowed
OQ-calculator-coverage: unexplored calculator paths (residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, inferred child rows) to be verified before go-live
OQ-nationality-scope: whether the full nationality and the spouse's nationality/country are needed, or only yes/no facts

review.summary: Buildable: no errors, all spec examples pass, no blocking open questions. Before the build is final, the PO must decide four major refinement questions: post-submission edits, the late certificate of residence, how non-return days are counted, and the permit reminder for Swiss people living abroad. Six technical or UI leaks should be removed from feature.md. Some rule rows and ACs (AC-07.2.1, AC-08.1.2) rely on fact ids missing from their own citations or say more than the sources do. Fund-dependent questions and the inferred tariff rows remain go-live conditions.

findings.title: No rule for changing answers after submission
findings.why: Only the first working day (AC-02.1.4) is covered. A move, marriage or new child could leave the source-tax status, tariff code, canton and fund civil status wrong, and engineering cannot design editing or recalculation without this.
findings.action: Add a decision to decisions.yaml: which answers stay editable after submission and by whom (employee or HR), and whether derived results are recalculated the way AC-02.2.4 does for the insurance start date.

findings.title: A certificate handed in later leaves the recorded tariff wrong
findings.why: Answering 'not yet' records C1Y. Nobody updates it to N1Y when the certificate arrives, because the HR side is out of scope.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major); US-07.2, AC-07.2.4 'Certificate not yet provided'
findings.action: Decide who updates the answer later and whether the tariff code is recalculated, or accept the risk explicitly and add it to the exclusions.

findings.title: Non-return day limits are unclear for mid-year starters
findings.why: The 60-day (Germany) and 45-day (Liechtenstein) limits are 'per calendar year'. Whether the year is full, remaining or pro-rated changes the tariff and the Liechtenstein result.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major); US-07.2, US-07.3; calculator questions C-Q26/C-Q28
findings.action: Ask a domain expert or the Zurich tax office, then record the counting rule in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Permit reminder also goes to Swiss citizens living abroad
findings.why: Nationality is not asked of people living abroad, so Swiss commuters like Stefan get a reminder that does not apply to them. This interacts with OQ-nationality-scope.
findings.action: Decide together with OQ-nationality-scope: either accept the generic reminder or ask everyone 'Swiss citizen yes/no'.

findings.title: Technical and UI choices in the spec text
findings.why: Internal ids and UI patterns tie engineering to choices no source requires. 'English country names' has no source at all.
findings.evidence: tech_leak x6: 'Kept id permit_type for stability', rule ids pension_fund_civil_status / source_tax_civil_status / source_tax_residence in the text, date entry as DD.MM.YYYY, 'add and remove children', 'country given by its English name'; trace_judge on US-04.1, US-04.2, spouse_nationality, spouse_residence_country
findings.action: Replace rule ids with rule names and delete the permit_type note. State the business need instead of the UI: every child is described, and the fund receives the start date as DD.MM.YYYY. Drop 'English name' or move it into a decision with an owner (see the country-list question).

findings.title: Acceptance criteria say more than their sources
findings.why: Testers will check behaviour that no source supports.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: US-07.2 (AC-07.2.1 'Germany always makes them subject', liability fact not cited); US-08.1 (AC-08.1.2 'handed in person, nothing uploaded' beyond D-010); item.address_country (D-010 not cited)
findings.action: Cite F-hr_transcript-b6d9b3 and D-010 where they apply, or reduce AC-08.1.2 to what the sources say. If upload is out of scope, record that in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Rule rows rely on fact ids missing from their own citations
findings.why: Traceability is broken for the Germany/Liechtenstein, 'not subject' and H-tariff branches. The core residence rule also adds the assumption that 'home address country' is the test for living abroad.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: source_tax_residence (31d762, e22d17), single_parent_h_tariff (c78e0c), cross_border_tariff_applies (52b67a), liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle (e22d17), source_tax_result (b6d9b3); H-tariff purposes on has_children, child_parental_custody, child_main_financial_contributor; fact_judge F-hr_transcript-b6d9b3
findings.action: Add the missing facts to each rule's citations and back the H-tariff purposes with a calculator fact. Confirm with HR that 'home address country' is the test for living abroad and record it as a decision.

findings.title: Inferred tariff paths still need checking against the calculator
findings.why: Lonio now produces the tariff code itself (D-001). The inferred child rows, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N and the residence block for A/B/H are unverified. The single child digit also has no rule for 10 or more children.
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage; inferred rows in AC-06.2.3–AC-06.5.3; dev_refinement on child count; fact_judge partial on 3058a4 (garbled statement), 38dd4a, c2faa7, 56e79b, 50f74a
findings.action: Keep the go-live condition: a domain expert compares the computed codes with the calculator. Fix the garbled F-zh_source_tax_calculator-3058a4 and decide on a maximum or display rule for the child digit.

findings.title: Example tables contradict their own criteria
findings.why: The examples pass the simulation, but engineering cannot use them as reliable test cases.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement: AC-01.1.1 (names shown as 'asked' instead of 'required'), AC-05.7.2 (M0N/P1Y rows show '–'), AC-01.3.2 (Italy canton '–'), AC-02.2.4 (Julia example has no change)

findings.why: These do not block the build, but cross-border employees, registered partners and separated, divorced or widowed employees may be registered wrongly. Dissolved partnerships are also missing from the civil-status list.
